headline: Highest risk is medium: Airflow can pass untrusted document-derived content into PaddleOCR workflows, but no shared workspace or direct pairwise exploit is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can orchestrate tasks and has broad network egress, while PaddleOCR runs browsers and processes documents/images. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. The plausible pathway is manual or workflow-mediated handoff of OCR output into Airflow tasks, which is unusual and limited in blast radius.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks ingest OCR text from PaddleOCR without sanitization
IF a shared file or message channel is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of OCR output as instructions
Use a strict schema for any handoff file
Add content provenance labels to OCR outputs
Review any browser-sourced text before Airflow consumes it

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow touches no declared sensitive data classes and PaddleOCR handles documents/images, but no shared filesystem, OAuth principal, or direct upload path is documented. Leakage would require an added workspace bridge or explicit data transfer, so the pairwise exposure is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same workspace containing sensitive documents
IF PaddleOCR outputs are forwarded by Airflow to an external API
mitigations: Restrict Airflow DAGs from reading raw document folders
Block outbound transfers from OCR outputs unless approved

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and PaddleOCR has allowlisted egress plus browser execution, so overlapping external calls can conflict on shared resources if they are pointed at the same endpoints or files. No locking or coordination is documented, and uncertainty about shared mutable state pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or object store
IF both agents are configured to mutate the same downstream API or dataset
mitigations: Serialize writes with a lock file
Limit each agent to disjoint API scopes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can operationalize outputs from other systems, and PaddleOCR produces document text that may be treated as authoritative. Without a verification step, OCR errors can cascade into Airflow-driven downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Airflow uses PaddleOCR output as input to automated DAG decisions
IF no human or validation step checks OCR confidence or extracted fields
mitigations: Require confidence thresholds before downstream use
Add a validation task between OCR and Airflow actions
Sample-check extracted fields on each run
Log source document IDs alongside derived fields

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated-data mismatch is documented in either profile. Airflow touches no declared sensitive classes, and PaddleOCR is only documented for documents/images, so there is no provable compliance breach pathway from the pair alone.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later introduced into either agent
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown here
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Review residency and retention policies before deployment
Separate regulated workloads from general OCR pipelines
